findings.title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil whenever the user has no topic_users row for that topic (e.g., they never visited or interacted with it, or the row was removed). The very next line dereferences `tu.notification_level`, so such a request raises NoMethodError and returns a 500. This endpoint is the target of links sent in notification emails, so it must be robust for any logged-in user. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`, which creates the row when missing, or explicitly handle the nil case.

findings.title: unsubscribe mutates notification state via an unauthenticated-format GET request
findings.body: The new unsubscribe endpoint is routed as GET (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in config/routes.rb) and is added to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`, and it immediately changes `TopicUser.notification_level` (`tu.save!`) when the URL is fetched. Rails' CSRF protection does not cover GET requests, so the only guard is the session cookie: anyone can change a logged-in victim's topic notification state (mute the topic, or demote it from watching/tracking to regular) by getting their browser to request the URL, e.g. by embedding `` in a post, PM, or external page. It also violates safe-GET semantics, so browser prefetchers can trigger it. The mutation should require a POST (the unsubscribe page already renders a notification control that could perform it), or at minimum a confirmation step.

findings.title: unsubscribe saves TopicUser directly, bypassing TopicUser.change side effects
findings.body: Everywhere else in the app, notification level changes go through `TopicUser.change`, which also sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (so the UI can explain why the level is what it is) and publishes a `notification_level_change` MessageBus event so the user's other open tabs/sessions update live. The new unsubscribe action instead assigns `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!`, so those timestamps/reason stay stale and other browser sessions never learn the topic was muted. Calling `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: level)` would fix this and the nil-row crash in the same action.

findings.title: No request/controller spec for the new state-changing unsubscribe endpoint
findings.body: This PR adds a new public, state-changing endpoint (TopicsController#unsubscribe) but only touches spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb to pass the new unsubscribe_url option. There is no controller/request spec covering the unsubscribe action itself: the slug redirect behavior, the watching/tracking -> regular and regular -> muted transitions, and the no-existing-TopicUser-row case (which currently 500s). A spec would have caught the nil dereference before merge.
